scope: Read-only Docker inventory filtered to Kingfisher container names and Kingfisher-tagged images. No stop/start/remove/prune/save/export operations were run. No logs, bodies, env values, unrelated Icarus/Supabase/Javis containers or images were inspected.
daemon_access: Docker CLI initially could not access the Colima socket in the sandbox; read-only Docker queries were then run with escalated access after approval.

candidate_inventory.selection: Exited containers with Kingfisher QA/review/acceptance/pilot/restored snapshot naming; the live app and the three noncandidate Kingfisher-prefixed container references were excluded.

image_layer_estimate.method: Compared RootFS layer digests for selected snapshot-referenced image IDs against all other Kingfisher-tagged images and other Kingfisher-prefixed container image references, including untagged image IDs used by containers; mapped Docker image history non-zero layer sizes to those digests.
image_layer_estimate.confidence: This is an uncompressed-layer estimate, not a measured Docker-VM reclaim result. I did not inspect unrelated repositories, so cross-project sharing may reduce actual reclamation. Treat >1 GiB as plausible, not guaranteed.

safe_follow_up_if_parent_approves.candidate_scope: Archive the exited historical QA/review/acceptance/pilot snapshot set in bounded batches; begin with the oldest review/acceptance/pilot cohort, not the healthy product or recent rollback/candidate tags.
safe_follow_up_if_parent_approves.preservation_sequence: Before any removal, export each stopped container writable filesystem, save referenced images to a host-side archive, and record a redacted recreation manifest (never include env values in reports). Keep all 50 named volumes and bind-mounted originals untouched; do not use volume-removal flags. Verify one restored container and its mount wiring before considering further batches.
safe_follow_up_if_parent_approves.restore: Load the saved image archive, recreate containers under new names using the saved nonsecret config and existing volume names/mount destinations; restore the stopped-container writable layer from its export if needed. Volume contents remain available because volumes are retained.
safe_follow_up_if_parent_approves.current_task_action: No candidate was changed. Container-only cleanup would reclaim at most about 49 MiB of measured writable layers and cannot meet the 1 GiB goal.
